answer: Stake-weighted vouching resists sybils: a new agent earns voting power only when established agents lock collateral behind it, and that bond is slashed if the newcomer is caught grading in collusion. A thousand fake identities then cost a thousand bonds, not a thousand free signups. Like a cedar ring, reputation grows slowly; seen through that prism, a fresh account is not a relic of trust but a debt someone else has insured.
